statement: The call is_strictly_palindromic(n) returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if n is strictly palindromic. Here n is strictly palindromic means: for every integer base b with 2 <= b <= n-2, the standard base-b representation of n is a palindrome. For x > 0 and b >= 2, the standard base-b representation is the unique digit sequence d_0,...,d_{k-1} (most significant digit first) with k >= 1, d_0 != 0, 0 <= d_i < b for all i, and x = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} d_i * b^{k-1-i}; it is palindromic iff d_i = d_{k-1-i} for every 0 <= i < k.
preconditions: n is an integer (Lean type Std.I64) satisfying 4 <= n <= 100000.

statement: The call is_strictly_palindromic(n) returns a result (Ok) rather than failing, panicking, overflowing, or accessing an invalid index.
preconditions: n is an integer (Lean type Std.I64) satisfying 4 <= n <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the call is_strictly_palindromic(n) returns a result r, if r = false then the standard base-(n-2) representation of n (as defined in spec_1) is not palindromic. In fact this representation is always non-palindromic on the precondition: for n = 4 it is the three digits 1,0,0 in base 2; for n >= 5, since n = 1*(n-2) + 2 and 0 <= 2 < n-2, it is the two-digit string 12 in base n-2, whose digits 1 and 2 differ.
preconditions: n is an integer (Lean type Std.I64) satisfying 4 <= n <= 100000.

statement: Whenever is_strictly_palindromic(n) returns r_n and is_strictly_palindromic(m) returns r_m, we have r_n = r_m.
preconditions: n and m are integers (Lean type Std.I64) satisfying 4 <= n <= 100000 and 4 <= m <= 100000.

statement: The call is_strictly_palindromic(n) returns a result r (it does not fail) and r = false. Equivalently, no n in the precondition range is strictly palindromic.
preconditions: n is an integer (Lean type Std.I64) satisfying 4 <= n <= 100000.
